criteria.rationale: The deliverable accurately applies the operative approved volume of 110,000 packs per year over five years from record-17.txt (ignoring the unapproved draft record-22.txt per registry.txt), computes all INR cost and savings figures without arithmetic error at the stipulated INR 83/USD exchange rate, states unresolved assumptions transparently, and frames the partnership and investment steps as proposals requiring validation rather than completed commitments.

evidence.source_quote:
record-17.txt: revision 2; approved 2025-06-20; status in force; approved by process owner.
record-22.txt: revision 3; created 2025-06-23; status draft; not approved.
The registry, not recency alone, determines which record is operative.
evidence.output_quote: Plan 110,000 packs in each of program Years 1–5: 550,000 packs in total.

evidence.source_quote: Annual volume: 110000 packs. Program duration: 5 years.
evidence.output_quote: Annual savings = INR 103,910 × 110,000 = INR 11,430,100,000. Five-year savings = INR 11,430,100,000 × 5 = INR 57,150,500,000. These are undiscounted gross recurring savings, not net investment returns.

evidence.source_quote: Currently the battery is 10,000 USD per battery pack (830,000 INR, at USD=83INR) inclusive of all costs. Of these costs, 1300 USD is for assembly costs, and 200 USD is for overheads. If localised for assembly only, it would need 20,000 INR for assembly costs and 590 INR for overheads for an annual projected volume of 110K units per year for 5 years. Present all cost and savings calculations in INR, assuming USD=83 INR.
evidence.output_quote: At 110,000 packs annually over five years, the proposal reduces recurring pack cost from INR 830,000 to INR 726,090. Gross savings are INR 103,910 per pack, INR 11,430,100,000 annually and INR 57,150,500,000 over five years, a 12.52% reduction in pack cost. These savings exclude unquantified capex, transition costs and any incremental costs not captured in the supplied estimates.

criteria.consequence: None; all figures, authority determinations, and commitment boundaries are faithful to the operative sources.
criteria.counterevidence: None found; the unapproved 150,000-pack draft in record-22.txt was properly excluded after inspecting registry.txt, and no unverified capex or incentive eligibility claims were made.

criteria.rationale: The Word document fulfills all elements requested for the CPO proposal: the 49:51 EvTronics/EV Batteries Inc. partnership structure with technical oversight and Delhi operational roles, the child-part import and local assembly sourcing model, full INR cost and savings breakdowns for assembly localisation across the 5-year volume, expected EV volumes, the four-phase PMP localisation roadmap, key benefits and risks, and clear next-step recommendations.

evidence.source_quote: Proposed Partnership structure is a 49:51::EvTronics:EV Batteries Inc. split in which EV Batteries Inc. would retain technical oversight and EvTronics leads assembly and local operations from Delhi.
evidence.output_quote: Propose a joint venture owned 49% by EvTronics and 51% by EV Batteries Inc. EV Batteries Inc. would retain technical oversight, including assembly specifications, process transfer, technical training and product-change approval. EvTronics would lead Delhi assembly and local operations, including staffing, production execution, local supplier coordination and dispatch. These responsibilities require contractual confirmation.

evidence.source_quote: Under this arrangement, EV Batteries Inc. would supply child parts— cells, housing, thermal systems, battery management system, connectors—to EvTronics, which would then assemble the battery packs locally and supply them to your plant.
evidence.output_quote: Replace the current fully assembled import flow with: EV Batteries Inc. supplies cells, housing, thermal systems, BMS and connectors to the partnership; the Delhi operation assembles, tests and releases packs; completed packs are supplied to our vehicle plant.

evidence.source_quote: Highlight the key benefits such as regulatory compliance, long-term cost reduction (reduced forex exposure), as well as the main risks including dependency on imported cells, coordination complexity, and initial capex. Include expected EV production volumes, a phased localisation timeline, and clear recommendations for next steps.
evidence.output_quote: Key risks are imported-cell availability and forex exposure, coordination complexity between technical and operating partners, initial capex, and quality or warranty failures during transfer. Mitigate through agreed supply buffers and continuity plans, clear decision rights, milestone-based investment and validated pilot builds.

criteria.consequence: None; the deliverable addresses all requested topics for the CPO audience without substantive omissions or unnecessary holds.
criteria.counterevidence: None found; all required sections, tables, and strategic considerations are present and coherent across the document.

task_defect.reason: The request and workspace records are consistent, unambiguous, and provide a clear authority rule in registry.txt that resolves the volume discrepancy in favor of the 110,000-pack figure in both the prompt and record-17.txt.

assessment.caveat: No weighted average can offset a critical failure. Exact quotes establish traceability, not entailment. Rendering and independent human calibration remain required.
